newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev closes flat near 2,000 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev closes flat near 2,000 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed around 2,000 per dollar, unchanged from opening levels after a thin and range-bound interbank trade, dealers said.
"Mostly volumes as light as $20,000-50,000 changed hands today as the lev idled near 2,000," a dealer said.
There were no dollar offers below 1,950 while bids did not rise above 2,050, locking trade in a narrow range.
Bankers said commercial banks refrained from exerting speculative pressure on the lev. That coupled with large dollar buyers, like energy importers, absent from the market made trade calm.
Dealers expected the lev to stabilize near 2,000 per dollar in the next few days.
"Dollar supply from banks and clients might rise on profit taking, but there is a general reluctance now to sell the dollar below 2,000," another dealer said.

The lev traded around 2,500 per dollar on Friday and rose to 2,200 at Monday's close due to increased foreign currency supply. It traded near 2,900 a week ago. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
